feat(mods): bin/advisor-mods-smoke - one-command live test of all mods

Runs each mod in a throwaway Claude Code session and prints PASS/FAIL:
write-gate (56KB Write denied, 1KB allowed, headless -p), canary (heartbeat
with endedAt for the session id), fleet-waker (interactive tmux: fake summon
discovered, one wake per unsynthesized result, no wake for a synthesized
one). Never touches ~/.advisor/runs; temp dirs and tmux sessions are always
cleaned up unless --keep. Exit 0/1/2/4, --only, --json, --timeout-scale.

The tmux pane runs in the tmux server's environment, so scrub vars are
removed with env -u in the pane argv (env K=V cannot unset); the pane
records its env after scrubbing and the check fails on any leak. Uses the
real child-session names (CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT, _CHILD_SESSION,
_ENTRYPOINT, _MESSAGING_SOCKET/_TOKEN, ...), not the doctrine's shorthand.

Verified: 40 unit tests; full live run 3/3 PASS (242s / 6s / 93s), no
leftover tmux sessions, pane env clean; advisor-audit-clis 0 unguarded;
bun test 1672 pass / 0 fail.

fix(runner,channel): end sentinel poll when the pane dies; reset stale Tail offsets

pollSentinel only checked liveness after its full timeout, so a runner whose
pane was killed (advisor-terminate / close-worker-tab) kept polling for up to

parsing a mid-line fragment (a plausible source of the stray
'malformed line: }' warning; not matched to a live occurrence).

fix(vault): stamp a review due_date on written lessons

writeLesson set type/created_at/task_type/polarity but never due_date, while
the surfacing machinery — listDue() and the SessionStart 14-day banner — keys
entirely off due_date. Any lesson written by the automated path was therefore
born invisible to review, permanently.

This was harmless until now only because the automated path had never run: all
34 notes in the lesson vault are hand-authored `manual-` files and exactly zero
were produced by writeLesson, which is the same dead-trigger story fixed in
94eaa57. Repairing that trigger makes this reachable — lessons are about to be
written for real, and every one would have been unreviewable.

Default horizon is 90 days via a named LESSON_DUE_HORIZON_DAYS constant; an
explicit record.due_date from the caller wins. 90d was chosen against the
observed created_at→due_date deltas on the 16 dated manual lessons, which
cluster at 14d/30d/92d.

The emitted value is a bare unquoted YYYY-MM-DD, matching what hand-authored
lessons store and what _upsertIndex feeds to listDue's lexical SQLite
comparison. A format listDue could not parse would be a silent no-op, so that
is covered end-to-end: a test asserts listDue() actually returns a freshly
written lesson, rather than merely asserting a string was written.

Existing lesson files are not retrofitted.

fix(channel): apply the complete-lines rule to recv, not just Tail

The previous commit fixed the trailing-partial warning in Tail.read and
deliberately left the whole-file reader alone, on the reasoning that a partial
line there meant genuine corruption. That reasoning was wrong: recv is
documented as a non-blocking read of a live append-only outbox, so a final
unterminated line is an in-progress write, exactly as in the Tail case.

Both readers now share one parseCompleteJsonLines helper rather than carrying
two near-identical loops that could drift. The final unterminated line is
skipped silently; a malformed line anywhere before it still warns and is still
skipped, with surrounding records returned normally.

fix(teardown): remove worktrees against the owning repo, not the advisor repo

_cleanup_worktree() derived its git root from the script's own location, so
`git -C "$advisorRoot" worktree remove` targeted the advisor repo no matter
which repo actually owned the worktree. For a worker summoned against an
external repo that removal silently failed — stderr goes to /dev/null — and
both the worktree and its ws/<sid> branch leaked in the external repo.

It now resolves the owning repo from meta.json's `repo` field, matching what
lib/channel.js synthesize already does, and falls back to advisorRoot when
meta.json is absent.

This was latent while `coder` was the only worktree agent. Widening the set to
doc-agent and planner in c258925 made it reachable on far more runs, so it is
fixed here rather than left.

Second, unrelated fix in the same teardown path: Tail.read advanced its byte
offset only past the last complete newline, but still fed the trailing partial
fragment to JSON.parse, printing a spurious "skipping malformed line" on nearly
every poll. No message was ever lost — the fragment is re-read intact on the
next read — but the noise buried real warnings. It now parses only complete
lines. A complete-but-corrupt line still warns; verified both ways.

fix(summon): isolate doc-agent and planner in their own worktrees

Workspace provisioning and $REPO were gated on `agent === 'coder'`, so every
other agent had $REPO pointing at the user's live main checkout. Earlier in
this session a doc-agent edited the live tree on master and reverted an
unrelated uncommitted file to satisfy a diff-scope check — it had no isolated
place to work.

WORKTREE_AGENTS (coder, doc-agent, planner) is now the single source of truth,
consumed by all four isolation sites and by the teardown gate in channel.js via
a lazy require. The teardown change is load-bearing, not cosmetic: that gate
also tested `agent === 'coder'`, so granting worktrees without it would leave a
.git/worktrees entry behind on every doc-agent and planner run.

The coder-only default timeout bump is deliberately NOT part of the set. It
reads the same way but is unrelated to isolation, and sweeping it in would give
planners and doc-agents coder-length timeouts.

Agents outside the set keep the copyDir template and $REPO === repo, so an
agent that needs to see uncommitted working-tree state still can — a worktree
is built from committed state and would hide it.

The bootstrap prompt now tells worktree agents their edits do not reach the
user's checkout and that deliverables must be copied to $OUTPUT_DIR.

Verified live, not just in tests: a real doc-agent summon produced
ws/<sid> with $REPO set to the worktree, and teardown left no stale entry.

fix(channel): re-wire lesson extraction to a reachable trigger

The LESSON EXTRACTION REQUIRED nudge was added in 35b4da9 gated on
`args.verdict === 'blocked' && args.material === 'yes'`, then deleted in
cf30392 as an unreachable guard. The deletion was correct — the guard could
never fire, for two independent reasons:

  1. Nothing ever passes --verdict. printSynthesisDirective emits a template
     with --sid/--seq/--established/--gap/--material/--next and no --verdict,
     so args.verdict was always undefined.
  2. material=yes contradicts verdict=blocked. `material` is the Advisor's
     answer to "is the remaining gap material?", and a blocked worker that
     delivered nothing is synthesized as material=no. The guard conflated a
     worker signal with an Advisor field.

But deleting it left the only worker-failure learning trigger as prose in
claude.md asking the Advisor to remember to run the skill. A self-healing
loop whose sole healing path is "the model remembers" does not heal.

The reachable signal was already in scope: synthesize reads the real worker
verdict off the persisted result envelope (persistResultMsg.body.verdict) a
few lines below where the dead block sat. The nudge now gates on that, and on
a blocked count >= 2 bounded by the same seq condition used to select the
envelope — one blocked verdict is noise, the second is signal.

The --verdict CLI flag remains entirely unread. The five existing tests still
pass unchanged (they seed no blocked envelope); their comments claimed the
block was permanently dead and have been corrected to say the flag is ignored
and the trigger is the persisted verdict.

Verified end-to-end: one blocked result prints nothing; a second prints a
runnable /extract-lesson command with --synthesis-log/--synthesis-seq/--agent,
matching the real skill contract, which has no --sid flag.

fix(brief-paths): stop reporting case-differing tracked paths as untracked

`git ls-files --error-unmatch` is case-sensitive even when core.ignorecase
is true — that setting governs git's working-tree comparisons, not this
plumbing command. A brief citing `CLAUDE.md` against a tree that tracks
`claude.md` therefore fell through to the untracked branch and was reported
invisible to the worker worktree, when in fact it is readable.

That inverts the checker's purpose: it exists to stop the Advisor briefing
workers on false premises, and here it manufactured one.

When core.ignorecase=true and the exact lookup misses, the cited path is now
resolved case-insensitively against the index. A match reports a visible,
non-blocking warning naming the real tracked casing, so the caller learns the
correct spelling instead of silently passing. Strict behaviour is preserved
when core.ignorecase is unset — on a case-sensitive filesystem a casing
mismatch is genuine invisibility. Downstream stale-vs-HEAD and commit-ancestry
checks operate on the resolved path.

Genuinely absent and gitignored paths still fail as before; no false negative
is introduced.

feat(brief-paths): catch briefs describing state the worker cannot see

Path visibility was necessary but not sufficient. Today a brief said "the fix
is now in place at lib/loop-bar.js" -- true in the advisor's checkout, but
UNCOMMITTED. Worker worktrees are created from committed state, so the worker
read HEAD's version, correctly found no fix, and returned BLOCKED. The old
check passed that brief cleanly: the file was tracked and not ignored.

What matters is whether the content the worker sees matches what the brief
describes. Two new decidable checks:

- Check A, stale vs HEAD (error, --warn downgradable): a cited tracked path
  whose content differs from HEAD. Catches staged and unstaged alike, since
  both are invisible from a fresh worktree.
- Check B, cited commits: a brief asserting "committed at <sha>" claims
  history the worker must see. Unresolvable -> error. Resolvable but not an
  ancestor of HEAD -> warning, since the object exists and git show works but
  the commit is absent from the worktree's history. The error/warning split
  follows advisor-check-doctrine and advisor-check-freshness.

Precision was the hard requirement, not recall: a noisy gate gets switched
off, which reproduces the failure it prevents. Check B only reads hex as a
commit claim when commit-context words appear nearby, and stays silent when
ambiguous. A test asserts a brief full of colour codes, ids and checksums
yields zero findings.

Verified against the original incident in all three states: unstaged dirty ->
exit 1, staged-not-committed -> exit 1, committed -> exit 0. Existing behavior
preserved (gitignored/nonexistent still exit 1, tracked-clean passes, --warn
downgrades, help-safe); JSON keys added, none renamed. Passes
bin/advisor-audit-clis. bun test: 1517 tests, 0 fail (7 new).
